dimensions.assessment: Affects specific federal and non-federal entities, including the Lewis and Clark Regional Water System, Inc. and regional authorities in Iowa, Minnesota, and South Dakota.
dimensions.evidence: expand the capacity and reach of the Lewis and Clark Regional Water System in the States of Iowa, Minnesota, and South Dakota.

dimensions.assessment: Involves conducting a feasibility study and reporting on whether a water supply project should be authorized, rather than directly constructing the project.
dimensions.evidence: carry out a study to determine the feasibility of the Lewis and Clark Regional Water Supply Project

dimensions.assessment: Limits federal expenditures for the study to $10,000,000, with a federal share not exceeding 50 percent.
dimensions.evidence: Not more than $10,000,000 of Federal funds may be expended to carry out the feasibility study

dimensions.assessment: Directs a specific agency study and reporting requirements to designated congressional committees without creating broad new general regulatory powers.
dimensions.evidence: carry out a study to determine the feasibility of the Lewis and Clark Regional Water Supply Project

dimensions.assessment: The authority provided by the section expires 5 years after the date of enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The authority provided by this section expires on the date that is 5 years after the date of enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Specific details on the exact total cost of the feasibility study beyond the federal cap.
Exact number of individuals or households that would eventually be served if the project is later built.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill directs the Secretary of the Interior to conduct a feasibility study for expanding the Lewis and Clark Regional Water System in Iowa, Minnesota, and South Dakota, with federal expenditures capped at $10 million and authority terminating after 5 years.
